## Classes

### <a name="clamav"></a>`clamav`

Installs the base package, with the command line scanner and the
libraries, from EPEL on the RedHat family. The daemons are managed by
their own classes, which include this one: clamav::clamd,
clamav::freshclam and clamav::milter.

The OS-specific defaults come from the module data.

#### Examples

##### The command line scanner only

```puppet
include clamav
```

##### The scanner daemon and its database updates

```puppet
include clamav::clamd
include clamav::freshclam
```

##### Add the ClamAV user to the group of an MTA filter

```puppet
class { 'clamav':
  manage_user => true,
  groups      => ['amavis'],
}
```

### <a name="clamav--clamd"></a>`clamav::clamd`

Installs clamd, writes its configuration and runs its service. The
configuration holds `default_options`, the options the packaged service
needs (socket, user, logging) from the module data, merged with
`options`. Every other option keeps the ClamAV default, see clamd.conf(5).

The file is checked by clamd before it is replaced, so an option unknown to
the installed ClamAV fails the Puppet run instead of the service.

#### Examples

##### Listen on TCP as well and raise the scan limits

```puppet
class { 'clamav::clamd':
  options => {
    'TCPSocket'   => 3310,
    'TCPAddr'     => '127.0.0.1',
    'MaxScanSize' => '400M',
    'MaxFileSize' => '100M',
    'ExcludePath' => ['^/proc/', '^/sys/'],
  },
}
```

### <a name="clamav--freshclam"></a>`clamav::freshclam`

Installs freshclam, writes its configuration and runs it. The
configuration holds `default_options`, the options the packaged service
needs from the module data, merged with `options`. Every other option
keeps the ClamAV default, see freshclam.conf(5).

The file is checked by freshclam before it is replaced.

freshclam runs either as a daemon checking for updates `Checks` times a
day (12 by default), or once a day from the `clamav-freshclam-once.timer`
systemd timer shipped by the packages, whose schedule can be changed. The
unit of the other mode is stopped and disabled.

#### Examples

##### Download through a proxy and tell clamd about new databases

```puppet
class { 'clamav::freshclam':
  options => {
    'HTTPProxyServer' => 'proxy.example.org',
    'HTTPProxyPort'   => 3128,
    'NotifyClamd'     => '/etc/clamav/clamd.conf',
  },
}
```

##### Update the databases every night at 3:30 from the systemd timer

```puppet
class { 'clamav::freshclam':
  mode        => 'timer',
  on_calendar => '*-*-* 03:30:00',
  timer_entry => { 'RandomizedDelaySec' => 0, 'AccuracySec' => '1min' },
}
```

### <a name="clamav--milter"></a>`clamav::milter`

Installs clamav-milter, writes its configuration and runs its service. The
configuration holds `default_options`, the sockets and user the packaged
service relies on from the module data, merged with `options`. Every other
option keeps the ClamAV default, see clamav-milter.conf(5). Unlike clamd
and freshclam, clamav-milter cannot check a configuration file without
starting, so the file is not validated.

The milter connects to the clamd sockets of `ClamdSocket`, by default the
local socket of clamav::clamd. The MTA must be able to reach
`MilterSocket`: on the RedHat family, the postfix user has to join the
clamilt group.

#### Examples

##### Reject infected mail

```puppet
class { 'clamav::milter':
  options => {
    'OnInfected' => 'Reject',
    'RejectMsg'  => 'Message rejected: infected by %v',
    'AddHeader'  => 'Replace',
    'LocalNet'   => ['local', '192.0.2.0/24'],
  },
}
```

##### Do not scan the mail of some addresses

```puppet
class { 'clamav::milter':
  allow_list => ['From:^postmaster@example\.org$', 'To:^abuse@'],
}
```

## Functions

### <a name="clamav--to_config"></a>`clamav::to_config`

Type: Puppet Language

Writes one `<Name> <value>` line per option, in alphabetical order, which
also puts `LogFileMaxSize` before `LogRotate` as ClamAV requires. An array
repeats the option once per value. Booleans are written `yes` and `no` and
undef options are left out.

#### `clamav::to_config(Clamav::Options $options)`

Writes one `<Name> <value>` line per option, in alphabetical order, which
also puts `LogFileMaxSize` before `LogRotate` as ClamAV requires. An array
repeats the option once per value. Booleans are written `yes` and `no` and
undef options are left out.

Returns: `String` The content of the configuration file.

##### `options`

Data type: `Clamav::Options`

The ClamAV options.

## Data types

### <a name="Clamav--Options"></a>`Clamav::Options`

The names are those of clamd.conf(5), freshclam.conf(5) and
clamav-milter.conf(5). An undef value leaves the option out of the file,
which removes a default of the module.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
{ 'MaxThreads' => 4, 'ScanPDF' => true, 'ExcludePath' => ['^/proc/', '^/sys/'], 'LogSyslog' => undef }
```

Alias of `Hash[Pattern[/\A[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\z/], Optional[Clamav::Value]]`

### <a name="Clamav--Value"></a>`Clamav::Value`

Booleans are written `yes` and `no`. An array repeats the option once per
value, for the options ClamAV accepts several times such as
`DatabaseMirror`, `ExcludePath` or `LocalNet`. A value cannot span several
lines.

#### Examples

##### 

```puppet
true
3310
'/run/clamav/clamd.ctl'
['^/proc/', '^/sys/']
```

Alias of `Variant[Boolean, Integer, Pattern[/\A[^\r\n]+\z/], Array[Variant[Integer, Pattern[/\A[^\r\n]+\z/]], 1]]`
